title: Positive Health Innovation – Development and piloting of a new dialogue on health promotion in primary care: Study protocol of a cluster-randomized proof-of-concept study
summary:
The “Positive Health Innovation” project is funded by the Federal Joint Committee's Innovation Fund. It started on January 1, 2025 with a duration of 36 months. The consortium is led by the “Institute for General Practice and Ambulatory Health Research (iamag)” at Witten/Herdecke University. The consortium partners are the Institute of General Practice, University Medicine Duisburg-Essen (Prof. Dr. Jürgen in der Schmitten); the Department of General Practice and Health Services Research, University Hospital Heidelberg (Prof. Dr. Attila Altiner); the Institute of General Practice, Centre for Health and Society (ifam/chs); Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (Prof. Dr. Stefan Wilm); the Department of Medical Informatics, Biometry and Epidemiology, Ruhr University Bochum (Prof. Dr. Nina Timmesfeld) and theInstitute of Health Economics and Clinical Epidemiology at the University of Cologne (Prof. Dr. Stephanie Stock).
The aim of the project is to develop and test an intervention to promote patient-centered dialogue in GP practices based on the Positive Health counseling concept developed in the Netherlands. A multimodal educational intervention approach based on the principles of the “peer approach” using existing regional network structures is chosen for the implementation of a new culture of conversation to improve the empowerment of GP patients receiving longitudinal care with high utilization. 
The potential of the Positive Health counseling concept will be analyzed and refined with regard to its application in German healthcare. A cluster-randomized proof-of-concept study in a stepped-wedge design will be conducted to assess the direct effects of this form of counselling on patient empowerment. The aim is to test whether a subsequent study with clinical endpoints would be feasible and promising.
conditions: Patients with longitudinal treatment with at least six doctor-patient contacts in the last three quarters

interventions.name: Intervention group: Two GP consultations according to the Positive Health approach
Control group: One consultation according to routine care (e.g. health check-up)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Longitudinal treatment with at least six doctor-patient contacts in the last three quarters 
- Appointment for one of the following consultations in the next three months: Health examination (check-up), follow-up in a disease management programme, basic psychosomatic care
Exclusion criteria:
- High degree of dementia, severe psychiatric or other illness which, according to a general practitioner's assessment, makes participation appear inadvisable, 
- Insufficient knowledge of the German language without the availability of language mediators.
